records.name: A deterministic selector induces a right-unique effective relation
records.statement: For any total selector sigma:X->X, the effective selector relation Sel_sigma(x,y) iff sigma(x)=y and y!=x is right-unique.
nonclaims: Right-uniqueness of the selector-induced relation does not make the underlying generic stepRel right-unique, terminating, or confluent.

records.name: Relation-sound selector iteration preserves base reachability
records.statement: If every non-fixed selector step sigma(u)=v is a stepRel(u,v), then every finite selector iterate sigma^k(x) is reachable from x by the reflexive-transitive closure of stepRel.
hypotheses: for all u, sigma(u)!=u implies stepRel(u,sigma(u))
nonclaims: Relation-soundness does not imply that selector iteration terminates or that all branches of stepRel follow the selector.

records.name: Natural-rank descent terminates deterministic selector iteration
records.statement: If rho:X->N and every non-fixed selector step strictly decreases rho, then selector iteration from x reaches a fixed point after at most rho(x) non-fixed steps.
hypotheses: for all u, sigma(u)!=u implies rho(sigma(u))<rho(u)
nonclaims: Termination under a declared natural-number rank does not establish confluence of the base relation or applicability to continuum and stochastic systems.

records.name: Sound rank-certified selectors give executable normalizers
records.statement: If a total selector is relation-sound, its fixed points are exactly the stepRel-normal states, and a natural-number rank strictly decreases on every non-fixed selector step, then deterministic selector iteration defines an executable normalizer that returns a reachable normal form for every input.
hypotheses: for all u, sigma(u)!=u implies stepRel(u,sigma(u))
for all u, sigma(u)=u iff u is stepRel-normal
for all u, sigma(u)!=u implies rho(sigma(u))<rho(u)
nonclaims: The returned selector normal form need not be the unique normal form reachable under the underlying relation when that relation branches.

records.name: Finite lexicographic recovery is unique with a final total tie-break
records.statement: For a finite nonempty candidate set, lexicographic minimization of a finite ordered objective tuple followed by a fixed total candidate order returns exactly one candidate.
hypotheses: the candidate set is finite and nonempty
each objective is defined on every candidate
the objective list is finite and ordered
the final tie-break is a fixed total order containing every candidate exactly once
nonclaims: A unique lexicographic selector result is a property of the declared objectives and tie-break contract, not a unique-selection theorem for the unspecialized relation or for nature.

records.name: Existential normalization is not an executable normalizer
records.statement: The terminating fork a->b and a->c has reachable normal forms b and c, so normal-form existence alone does not specify which normal form an executable recovery procedure must return.
records.fixture: three-state terminating fork with two distinct normals and no selector
nonclaims: The fixture does not prevent adding a separately declared deterministic selector; it shows that the relation alone does not contain one.

records.name: Deterministic does not imply relation-sound
records.statement: A total deterministic selector can map a to c even when the declared base relation contains only a->b, so determinism alone does not make selector steps licensed relation steps.
records.fixture: selector sigma(a)=c over base relation containing only a->b
nonclaims: The counterexample concerns relation soundness only; an unrelated deterministic function remains a valid function.

records.name: A relation-sound deterministic selector can loop
records.statement: On the two-cycle 0->1->0, the deterministic selector sigma(0)=1 and sigma(1)=0 is relation-sound but never reaches a fixed point.
nonclaims: The fixture does not refute termination when a valid well-founded progress certificate is supplied.

records.name: Objective minimization without a total tie-break can remain set-valued
records.statement: If two finite recovery candidates have identical values for every declared objective and no final total tie-break is supplied, objective minimization leaves both candidates tied and does not define a unique selector result.
records.fixture: two candidates with equal objective tuples and no final total order
nonclaims: Equal objective values are not a defect; the counterexample rejects only an undeclared promotion from a tied argmin set to a unique selector.

records.name: A deterministic selector does not make the base relation confluent
records.statement: Adding a selector that chooses b on the fork a->b and a->c yields a deterministic terminating selector path to b while c remains a distinct reachable normal form of the base relation, so selector determinism does not prove base-relation confluence or unique normal form.
records.fixture: three-state fork with selector choosing one branch
nonclaims: The selector specialization may intentionally choose one branch; it simply must not rewrite the semantics of the underlying relation.

claim_boundary: GENERIC_RELATION != DETERMINISTIC_SELECTOR; EXISTENTIAL_NORMALIZATION != EXECUTABLE_NORMALIZER; TERMINATING_SELECTOR != BASE_RELATION_CONFLUENT; EXECUTABLE_NORMALIZER != EMPIRICAL_RECOVERY
